focus: Memory that stays correct when facts change.
Comparing retire, delete, and decay on facts that change more than once.
Scoring the update step itself, not only the final answer.

topics.name: How memory is organized
topics.standing: Designs moved from flat lists ranked at read time to structure built at write time. No same-condition test of which structure matters.

topics.name: Updating and forgetting
topics.standing: Mem0 and Zep make updates explicit, but only Zep is tested on knowledge-update questions, with mixed results.

topics.name: Evaluating memory
topics.standing: Each system uses a different benchmark, and even on shared ones the papers disagree on labels and re-run scores.

topics.name: Memory vs. long context
topics.standing: Full context wins or ties on short histories; memory wins at about 115K tokens, and on latency everywhere.

papers.title: Generative Agents
papers.oneLine: A memory stream ranked by recency, importance, and relevance, plus reflection.

papers.title: MemoryBank
papers.oneLine: Summaries, a user portrait, and an Ebbinghaus forgetting curve for companion chat.

papers.title: MemGPT
papers.oneLine: The LLM pages memory between its context and external storage, like an OS; introduces DMR.

papers.title: LoCoMo
papers.oneLine: Benchmark of 50 months-long conversations; models fall far behind humans on temporal questions.

papers.title: LongMemEval
papers.oneLine: Benchmark of 500 questions over ~115K-token histories, including knowledge updates.

papers.title: Zep
papers.oneLine: A temporal knowledge graph that retires old facts with a valid-time; beats full context on LongMemEval.

papers.title: A-MEM
papers.oneLine: Zettelkasten-style linked notes that the LLM keeps rewriting.

papers.title: Mem0
papers.oneLine: Extracted facts with ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, and NOOP decided by the LLM; full context still scores higher on LoCoMo.
